chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Hamzah al-Qummi, from Muhammad ibn Khalaf, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about eating the meat of the khazz (a type of aquatic animal), and he said: 'It is the dog of the water; if it has a fang, do not approach it (eat it), and if not, then approach it (eat it).'

And Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi narrated to me from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Humran ibn Ayn, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the khazz, and he said: 'It is a beast that grazes on land and rests in the water.'

key_terms.الْخَزِّ: Khazz, a type of aquatic or semi-aquatic animal (often identified as beaver or otter)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of the khazz according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the fiqh of hunting semi-aquatic mammals by distinguishing between those with prominent fangs, which are generally avoided, and those without, which are permissible. The narration highlights the practical methodology of the Imams in categorizing animals based on observable physical traits and habitat, reflecting the Shia emphasis on deriving legal rulings from clear, tangible indicators. This specific ruling on 'khazz' serves as a key example in the chapter of hunting, illustrating how subtle biological distinctions impact dietary laws.
